title: Doubling and halving
examples: If I have ten sweets, what is half?
Can you share six apples between two friends?

explain.say: Let us learn about doubling numbers today. Doubling means making two equal groups. We take a number and count it two times.
For example, if we double the number two. We have two fingers in one group. We have two fingers in another group. That makes four.
Next we look at doubling up to ten. Double of three is six. Double of four is eight. Double of five is ten.
Now we learn about halving numbers. Halving means sharing something into two equal groups. We take a number and split it in two.
Let us halve the number ten. We put ten counters in one pile. We share them equally into two piles. Each pile has five counters.

faq.q: What does it mean to double a number?
faq.a: It means to multiply that number by two. You are making two equal groups of that number.
asks: How do I double this number?

faq.a: You can only halve even numbers perfectly. An even number can be shared equally into two groups.
asks: What if the number is odd?
Is there a number I cannot halve?

faq.q: Is halving the same as dividing by two?
faq.a: Yes, it is exactly the same thing. Halving a number means dividing it by two.
asks: What is the math word for sharing in two?

faq.q: How do I know if a number is even?
faq.a: A number is even if it can be shared equally into two groups. You can check if it ends in zero, two, four, six, or eight.
asks: Are all numbers that end in two even?

faq.q: What is the difference between doubling and halving?
faq.a: Doubling is going up by two times the amount. Halving is going down by sharing it into two equal parts.
asks: Is doubling the opposite of halving?
If I double and then halve, what happens?

facts: Doubling a number means multiplying it by two.
Halving a number means dividing it by two.
If you double a number and then halve it, you get the original number back.
Only even numbers can be perfectly halved using whole numbers.

quiz.why: You count four fingers in one group and four fingers in another group. That makes eight.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you only counted the number once, not twice.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you multiplied four by four, not by two.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you only wrote the number down once.

quiz.why: When you share sixteen items equally into two groups, each group gets eight items.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you did not share the items into two groups.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you subtracted one instead of dividing by two.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you multiplied sixteen by ten.

quiz.say: If you have ten stickers and share them equally between two friends, how many does each friend get?
quiz.why: Sharing ten stickers equally means putting five stickers with one friend and five stickers with the other friend.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you added two extra stickers.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you did not share the stickers at all.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only counted the number of friends.
